notes: Connecting a project to an empty GitHub repository now offers Initialize and push even when an earlier failed attempt left an empty .git folder behind, instead of reporting a conflict.

Initialize and push now has a review step: "Review files" lists what would be uploaded (your .gitignore is honoured) with the file count and total size, and flags large files, likely secrets such as keystores and keys, log and crash files, and build or cache folders. You tick what to leave out and choose whether to add it to the project's .gitignore or exclude it on this machine only. Nothing is committed until you confirm. Available in the web dashboard and the Android app.

Initialize and push, Commit and downloading a repository no longer fail on a big project: git add, commit and download are now allowed to run for minutes instead of being stopped after 4 seconds. The stopped command used to leave a stale lock file in the project's .git folder and every later attempt failed; a lock that is minutes old is now cleared automatically.
When a git step fails, the message now shows Git's real error instead of hundreds of line-ending warnings.

Initialize and push: the check for large files now counts only the files that would really be uploaded, so a project's own .gitignore is honoured. A big build output inside an ignored folder (for example app/build/) no longer blocks initializing a repository.

Projects without a folder: a project can now be created with no folder (tick "This project has no folder"). It can only be started, stopped and tunnelled, which suits something that already runs elsewhere, such as a Docker Desktop container. Features that need a folder (Git, .env, scripts, Studio) are switched off for it.
Clearer messages when inspecting a repository: a non-empty folder, a git folder with no GitHub connection, and a GitHub access refusal each now explain what to do next.

Crash history: the Agent now records every time a project's process ends without being stopped (when, exit code, how long it had been running, whether it was started again, and the last lines of its output). See it from the project's menu in the web dashboard and in the Android app.
Docker: a new panel in the web dashboard and the Android app lists the containers on the machine, lets you start, stop or restart one, and shows its latest output. Only the machine owner can use it.
Updating the Agent now stops and starts again only the projects that have a database attached (those are the ones that needed it). Projects without a database keep running through the update.

Studio now stays in step across your devices: when you answer a question (approve a command, a plan or a Codex approval) on one device, the other devices drop it too, and a task started on one device shows up as running on the others and finishes there as well.
Updating the Agent no longer closes your public tunnels for good: the tunnels that were open are opened again after the update (a quick tunnel gets a new public address from its provider).

Updating the Agent no longer leaves your projects half-working: before the update the Agent stops the projects it started (and their database, if it is set to stop with the project), and starts them again right after the update. Before this, a project could look Running after an update but stop responding until you pressed Stop and Start.
A running Studio task can now be watched from more than one device at once (for example your phone and a browser): every step, question and the final reply appear on all of them.
Studio edits that you review before saving now go through the Agent's change approval from the Android app too, so the Agent keeps an undo snapshot and a history entry for them.
New session with a handoff for long Studio chats (web and Android app): the new session starts with automatic notes about the goal, decisions, files and next step, and the old chat stays in History.
For Codex, starting a new session now also starts a fresh Codex thread, so a very long Codex conversation no longer carries on in the background.
You can now change or disconnect a project's GitHub repository from the project settings (web and Android app). Disconnecting only removes the link: your files, commits and branches are not touched.
A model test (the "hi" sent to each model on the AI providers screen) is no longer treated as a finished task, so it no longer makes the project show "finished" or trigger a notification.
When thinking is switched off in Studio, local Ollama models that can think no longer think anyway. This avoids long hidden reasoning and replies that were cut off.
Agent mode can now read big files page by page (start_line / end_line), so a model is no longer stuck on the first 4,000 characters of a large file.
The model is told which operating system the machine runs, so it stops guessing from error messages.
Reading PDF files in Studio now works in the packaged Agent on Linux and Windows.
Local Ollama is no longer hidden from Studio when no custom address is saved.
A single bad CPU or memory sample can no longer spike the metrics chart.
The owner can set a custom address for local Ollama in Studio.
When a Linux restart or shutdown fails, the message points to the in-app setup guide.
A failed Linux restart or shutdown now points to the setup guide.
New restart and shutdown actions for the machine itself.
Word documents are recognised as a previewable document type in Studio.
With debug logging on, the Agent records a periodic memory snapshot to help find leaks.
Windows self-update is more reliable: the update helper is started through cmd so it is not stopped together with the Agent.
The Agent never recursively watches an external project folder or a bare drive root.
Studio chat history backups: an empty snapshot can no longer overwrite a good one, restore uses the new file names, and backups include the key that protects the history.
Self-update now uses a signed PowerShell helper on Windows and a fixed shell helper on Linux and macOS.
Studio can show a short "what it is doing now" line for a running turn without opening the chat.
